A reply counts as confirmed if the mail server marked the message as answered, or a sent message linked to the request by In-Reply-To or by the same thread was found. The SLA is counted in working minutes on the selected schedule when the request or the reply arrived during working hours. If both the request and the reply fall outside the schedule, the reply is credited to the employee but the SLA is not evaluated; the actual time is shown for reference. Such replies are listed separately and excluded from the SLA totals. A reply after the end of the period is counted if the request arrived within the selected period. One message can carry several labels, so category rows do not add up. The mail archive stores the current category but not when it was assigned, so the report cannot reconstruct the exact moment a request was picked up. Missing history or an unsynchronised account makes the report incomplete.
